title: When the Cipher Falls Revisited
premise: Casper Whitlock, the unofficial fixer for a deniable embassy operation called the Meridian Desk, is ordered to scrub a charter flight from every database while it's still airborne. When the plane lands carrying a passenger who officially never existed—her presumed-dead mentor, Elias Vane—Casper learns the vanishing records were a rehearsal for a larger erasure: a staged industrial disaster meant to bury evidence of a weapons program her own agency helped build. Torn between loyalty to the Desk that made her and the truth Vane died protecting, she assembles an unlikely crew of exiles, forgers, and a defector analyst to expose the attack before it's disguised as an accident. The novel ends with Casper choosing truth over the institution, leaking the archive at the cost of her own official existence—and finding, in her ragtag crew, the family the Desk never was.
about_author: Ulyana Oyelaran is a former logistics analyst who spent six years in West African port cities before turning to fiction, where she writes about people who move in the gaps between official records. She lives in Lisbon with a rescue dog named Cipher and a healthy distrust of paperwork.

chapters.title: The Go-Bag Rule
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. A routine night at the Meridian Desk: Casper erases a diplomat's drunk driving, checks her packed bag, and recites her polished cover story to a new colleague. The emotional beat is controlled loneliness—she's competent, invisible, and quietly proud of it, unaware how fragile that invisibility is.

chapters.title: Flight 4471, Still Airborne
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Orders come down: wipe every trace of charter flight 4471 while it's mid-Atlantic. Casper executes flawlessly, then notices the manifest lists a name she buried years ago. The beat is dread blooming inside routine—her first crack in the polished lie.

chapters.title: The Man Who Wasn't on the Manifest
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. She meets the plane at a fogged-in airfield and finds Elias Vane—her mentor, officially dead for six years—half-conscious and clutching a data shard. He gives her one sentence: 'They're rehearsing your funeral.' Beat: shock curdling into protective fury.

chapters.title: Deniable Assets
chapters.summary: Vane's flashback POV, six years earlier. He discovered the Kestrel Program—a weapons system disguised as humanitarian logistics—and chose to die rather than hand it over. Beat: the origin of Casper's grief and the inheritance she never knew she received.

chapters.title: The Desk Calls
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Her director, Imogen Sarr, gently orders her to surrender the shard and take mandatory leave. Casper complies—then copies the shard first. Beat: the moment loyalty and truth split into two different roads.

chapters.title: People in the Gaps
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. She calls in favors from the margins: Noor, a forger who owes her a life; Dez, a disgraced air-traffic analyst; and Tomas, a smuggler with a grudge against Kestrel's contractor. Beat: the first stitches of found family, stitched from debts and distrust.

chapters.title: Reading the Shard
chapters.summary: Noor and Dez's alternating POV. The shard decrypts in fragments: a schedule, a site code, and a rehearsal log proving the flight erasure was a drill for something bigger. Beat: exhilaration of discovery undercut by the realization the Desk is inside the plot.

chapters.title: The Accident Calendar
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Cross-referencing site codes reveals a pattern of 'accidental' disasters across three continents—all covering Kestrel test failures. The next entry is dated eleven days out, at a refinery outside Rotterdam. Beat: cold arithmetic of lives reduced to line items.

chapters.title: Sarr's Kindness
chapters.summary: Imogen Sarr's POV. Sarr is not a cartoon villain: she believes burying Kestrel prevents a war. She assigns a cleaner team to retrieve the shard 'gently.' Beat: the antagonist's tragic logic, and the reader's first doubt about who the real enemy is.

chapters.title: Safehouse Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Holed up in Noor's Rotterdam loft, the crew argues about going to the press versus the Desk's internal watchdog. Casper's old instincts say trust the institution; Vane's shard says otherwise. Beat: the family's first real fight, and first real bond.

chapters.title: The Cleaner's Waltz
chapters.summary: Dez's POV. A Desk cleanup team hits the loft; the crew escapes through canal rooftops, but Tomas is taken. Beat: adrenaline and guilt—Casper learns that keeping people close means giving the enemy leverage.

chapters.title: What Tomas Knew
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV, in custody. Interrogated by a Desk officer he once called friend, he gives up nothing but buys time with a planted lie about the shard's location. Beat: loyalty as a weapon wielded from the bottom of the board.

chapters.title: Vane's Second Grave
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Following Vane's contingency instructions, she exhumes a dead-drop in a cemetery annex: his full Kestrel dossier and a letter naming his killer inside the Desk. Beat: grief transmuted into inheritance; she stops mourning and starts aiming.

chapters.title: The Name in the Letter
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. The letter names Deputy Director Hale—Sarr's superior—as Kestrel's architect, using Sarr as a deniable shield. The crew realizes stopping Sarr won't stop the attack. Beat: vertigo of scale; the conspiracy is taller than its visible face.

chapters.title: Eleven Becomes Four
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. The attack date moves up; the refinery 'accident' is now four days away, timed to a shareholder summit that Hale will attend remotely. Beat: the floor drops out—planning time is gone, only improvisation remains.

chapters.title: Borrowing the Desk
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. She walks back into the Meridian Desk wearing her polished lie, uses her access to pull the refinery's safety overrides, and confronts Sarr with the letter. Beat: loyalty vs. truth made flesh—she offers Sarr a chance to be a whistleblower instead of a scapegoat.

chapters.title: Sarr's Choice
chapters.summary: Sarr's POV. Torn between the institution that raised her and Hale's proof of her expendability, Sarr gives Casper the summit's security architecture—then stays behind to burn her own trail. Beat: tragic solidarity between two women built by the same machine.

chapters.title: Four Hours at the Refinery
chapters.summary: Casper and Dez's alternating POV. The crew infiltrates the refinery to trigger a harmless shutdown and force an evacuation order that makes the 'accident' impossible to stage quietly. Beat: white-knuckle competence—everything Casper learned as a fixer turned against the fixers.

chapters.title: The Erasure Reversed
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. While Casper holds the control room, Noor broadcasts the Kestrel archive to forty newsrooms and three tribunals, making the attack too visible to bury. Beat: triumph as an act of publication—the opposite of everything Casper's old job required.

chapters.title: Hale's Last Audit
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Hale corners Casper in the refinery; Sarr's delayed signal and Dez's rigged shutdown turn Hale's escape route into his exposure—he's arrested arriving at a disaster that never happens. Beat: climax and catharsis; the eraser erased.

chapters.title: The Price of a Name
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. In the fallout, the Desk disavows her; her records, passports, and history are dissolved—the erasure she once performed is turned on herself. Sarr, exiled too, offers her a place in a new oversight unit. Beat: bittersweet freedom; she has lost the lie and kept the truth.

chapters.title: Packed Light
chapters.summary: Casper's POV, epilogue. Months later in Lisbon, Casper still keeps a go-bag—now packed for a family road trip with Noor, Dez, and a recovering Tomas. The final beat: inheritance redefined; what Vane left her wasn't the dossier, it was the choice, and she finally unpacked the fear.
